newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian investors take U.S. data as excuse to sell.
newsitem.headline: Belgian investors take U.S. data as excuse to sell.

text.p: A raft of strong U.S. data on Friday provided the excuse Belgian investors have been waiting for to sell, pushing the Bel-20 index down 1.68 percent.
Dealers said the move's strength and scale took them by surprise. At one point around 1400 GMT the index was down more than 2.50 percent, but late buying lifted most stocks from their lows.

Profit taking began on a stronger-than-expected rise in U.S. non-farm payrolls. But that turned to panic selling when a rise in the U.S. national association of purchasing managers (NAPM) index sent bonds falling and the Dow .DJI down 100 points.
By 1530 GMT, an hour after the Belgian market's close, the Dow had narrowed its loss to around 60 points.
One Ghent-based trader said he believed the down move had been overdone but a recovery in Belgian stocks on Monday would depend on the Dow's performance in the rest of the U.S. session.

"I don't think there's any reason to sell off at the moment," he added. While there was some short term pressure on interest rates because of fears about a Bundesbank reaction to a weak mark, European economies were still in slow speed, he said.
While the U.S. data hit stocks across the board, most of Friday's session was focused on company earnings news.
Oil and gas group PetroFina managed to buck the downtrend, rising 2.67 percent to 15,400 francs, thanks to a 61 percent rise in first half profits.
Shares in PetroFina shareholders Electrafina, GBL and Sofina also rose.
Chemicals maker Solvay suffered however on disappointment at its first half profit rise of three percent. Solvay ended down 2.54 percent at 23,000 francs.
Shares in Solvay's main shareholder Solvac, which is controlled by descendants of the company's founder, fell 3.17 percent.
Other heavy blue chip losers included bank BBL, cement maker CBR and steel wire maker Bekaert.
Among the small caps, data communications company Telinfo added 20 francs to 2,020 francs ahead of the release of first half 1997 earnings.

After the close, Telinfo said group net profit rose 26 percent in the six months to June 30, although pre-tax current profit rose by only six percent. The company reiterated it was looking to make acquisitions and said also results at its 10-percent owned Mobistar mobile phone unit were strong.
